definition: What it costs to buy the device that carries AI access in Africa: published average selling prices, entry-level price bands, and the volume and price movements around them. Prices are recorded in the currency and period reported by the source.

type_key.projection: Analyst projection for the current year

observations.note: Legit.ng reported Omdia's February 2026 forecast of an approximately 23% to 25% annual shipment decline. Omdia's later Q2 outlook revised the full-year estimate to -26%; this earlier forecast is retained as dated reporting, not the current outlook.
Proposed 25% excise duty, which would land directly on device prices. Proposed 25% excise duty, assessed at activation, which would land directly on device prices.
South Africa's smartphone shipments grew 17% year on year in 1Q26. The same Omdia release reports Africa overall +3% and Nigeria +8%.
TechCabal reports Omdia's projection that component-cost pressure could raise Nigerian smartphone prices by up to 30% in 2026; this is a forecast, not a measured price index.

A secondary report attributes increases of up to 40–50% in some emerging markets to IDC, but does not identify countries, price bases or a comparable sample. Retained as a quarantined regional report; no country-level value is inferred.
TrendForce forecast conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 58–63% quarter on quarter and NAND Flash 70–75% in 2Q26. This is a contract-price forecast, not a realised consumer-device price change.

Telecompaper reports Omdia's 26% full-year 2026 decline forecast. The Omdia primary URL is retained in original_source_url but has no retrievable Wayback snapshot; this secondary-source row is quarantined from headline use.

Telecompaper's public report preview attributes a 34% 2Q26 decline, nearly 3 million units, in Africa's sub-$100 segment to Omdia. The Omdia primary URL is retained in original_source_url but has no retrievable Wayback snapshot; this secondary-source row is quarantined from headline use.

Telecompaper reports Omdia's estimate that African smartphone shipments fell 7% year on year in 2Q26. The Omdia primary URL is retained in original_source_url but has no retrievable Wayback snapshot; this secondary-source row is quarantined from headline use.

TechCentral reports NielsenIQ's H1 2026 South African smartphone average selling prices rose 9.8% year on year while unit volumes fell 7.9%. This is a retail-sales mix measure, not a controlled device-price index.
IDC forecasts a worldwide 2026 smartphone average selling price of $581, up 27.6% year on year, revised from $550.
Counterpoint reports existing smartphone prices up 15% globally on average so far in 2026; new launches 25% costlier year on year; Middle East & Africa up 18%.
Legit.ng reviewed current Nigerian retail listings and reported budget-phone prices across the ₦100,000–₦300,000 range on 29 August 2026. These are sampled listings, not a national price index.
